title: A Few Surprises
summary: Most rules behave as expected, but these few cases surprise almost everyone.
lesson: Rules cover actions, not outcomes, so allow what you need rather than blocking what you fear.
oneLiner: Most rules behave as expected, but these few cases surprise almost everyone.
explain: A rule blocks one action, not an outcome. WETH turns any ETH sent to it into wrapped ETH, even without its wrap action.
Removing a rule does not block anything: the action falls to Anything else. A failed batch gives back any one-time permission it used.
A delegatecall lets another contract run its code as if it were the Safe, with full control. Never allow unknown code to do that.
takeaway: Rules cover actions, not outcomes, so allow what you need rather than blocking what you fear.

steps.label: Wrap 1 ETH
steps.note: Wrapping has its own rule, Always Deny, so this is blocked.

steps.label: Send 1 ETH to WETH
steps.note: WETH wraps any ETH it receives. A plain send has no rule of its own, so Anything else allows it.

steps.label: Send Dave 1 ETH with four zero bytes attached
steps.note: Four zero bytes look like an empty send, so they reach Dave's plain ETH rule. The Plain ETH Transfer policy notices; Always Allow would not.

steps.label: Run unknown code inside the Safe
steps.note: This is a delegatecall. Anything else here covers normal calls only, so unknown code gets no way in.
